assessment.rationale: The RFC establishes that servers are general-purpose and support many contexts, but does not state that they 'must support' GET and POST as a mandatory requirement under the June 2022 standard.
assessment.provenance_note: RFC 9110 introduction states servers are general-purpose and reusable across contexts.
limitations: No explicit mandate for GET/POST methods in the RFC text reviewed

excerpts.text: Much of that architecture is reflected in the terminology used to define HTTP.[¶](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110/#section-3-1)

assessment.rationale: Span 203 states 'Most HTTP communication consists of a retrieval request (GET)'. It does not state that GET is required as a mandatory method for all general-purpose servers under the June 2022 HTTP standard.
assessment.provenance_note: RFC 9110 section 3.6 describes typical GET usage but not as a requirement.
limitations: No explicit requirement stated for GET method support

excerpts.text: Most HTTP communication consists of a retrieval request (GET) for a representation of some resource identified by a URI.
